correctness.rationale: Independent-edge coupling is exact on finite trees. The low-p coefficient follows from one successful adjacent edge. The near-one coefficient follows from single-edge failure, with two-failure errors O((1-p)^2). The identity sum s_e^2=nD_v-W is proved by edge-pair counting. Farness increases from any nonleaf toward at least one branch with fewer than n/2 vertices. Uniform polynomial expansions on a finite vertex set imply strictly disjoint argmax sets. Explicit P3 variance factorization gives the unique sharp transition. Exact independent polynomial checker covers every root of every unlabeled tree with 3..9 vertices; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Maximal outbreak-size uncertainty is a natural risk-sensitive epidemic-source objective, distinct from mean size or duration. The result gives a universal, not sampled-graph-specific, forced change of maximizer, a structural bridge from single-edge outbreak severance to classical Wiener/farness invariants, and an exact sharp minimal example. It quantifies why weak- and strong-transmission source rankings are irreconcilable on every nontrivial contact tree; useful in sensitivity analysis of finite contact structures. No claims of novel percolation correspondence or broader heterogeneous SIR theory.
